When every class lists its members in the same order, you know where to look: fields at the top, then the constructor, then the methods. Without an agreed order, a field declared between two methods is easy to miss.

By default the order is: index signatures, call signatures, fields, static blocks, constructors, `accessor` properties, getters, setters, methods. Within each kind, static members come first, then decorated, instance and abstract ones. Within each of those, `public` comes before `protected`, `private` and `#private`.

A field with a function as its value counts as a method.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
class Timer {
  start(): void {}

  constructor() {}

  private elapsed = 0;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
class Timer {
  static readonly limit = 60;
  private elapsed = 0;

  constructor() {}

  get seconds(): number {
    return this.elapsed;
  }

  start(): void {}
  stop = (): void => {};
}
```

## Options

The rule takes one object. Each key sets the order for one kind of container.

| Option | What it applies to |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Everything that doesn't have its own setting. |
| `classes` | Class declarations. |
| `classExpressions` | Class expressions. |
| `interfaces` | Interfaces. |
| `typeLiterals` | Type literals such as `type Point = { ... }`. |

Each value is `"never"` (don't check), a list of member groups, or an object:

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memberTypes` | `"never"`. Under `default`, the order above | The groups, in the order you want them, or `"never"` to ignore groups. |
| `order` | `"as-written"` | How to sort inside a group: `"alphabetically"`, `"alphabetically-case-insensitive"`, `"natural"`, `"natural-case-insensitive"`. |
| `optionalityOrder` | not set | `"required-first"` or `"optional-first"`. |

A group is a kind of member: `signature`, `readonly-signature`, `call-signature`, `field`, `readonly-field`, `static-initialization`, `constructor`, `accessor`, `get`, `set`, `method`. In classes you can narrow it with an accessibility, a scope, or both: `private-field`, `static-method`, `public-static-method`, `protected-abstract-get`, `decorated-field`.

- A member goes in the most specific group that's listed.
- A member that doesn't fit any listed group can go anywhere.
- Groups in an inner list have the same rank.

Methods before fields:

{/* good {"options": [{"default": ["method", "constructor", "field"]}]} */}
```ts
class Timer {
  start(): void {}

  constructor() {}

  private elapsed = 0;
}
```

Only sort by name:

{/* bad {"options": [{"default": {"memberTypes": "never", "order": "alphabetically"}}]} */}
```ts
interface Point {
  y: number;
  x: number;
}
```

`"natural"` compares numbers inside names by value, so `item2` comes before `item10`:

{/* good {"options": [{"default": {"memberTypes": "never", "order": "natural"}}]} */}
```ts
interface Row {
  item2: string;
  item10: string;
}
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"default": {"memberTypes": "never", "order": "alphabetically"}}]} */}
```ts
interface Row {
  item2: string;
  item10: string;
}
```

Required members first:

{/* bad {"options": [{"default": {"memberTypes": "never", "optionalityOrder": "required-first"}}]} */}
```ts
interface User {
  nickname?: string;
  name: string;
}
```

Check classes only:

{/* good {"options": [{"default": "never", "classes": ["field", "method"]}]} */}
```ts
interface Store {
  save(): void;
  size: number;
}
```
